classFeature.name: Rage
entries: In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can enter a rage as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} if you aren't wearing {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.
While raging, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength checks and Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.

When you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} using Strength, you gain a bonus to the damage roll that increases as you gain levels as a berserker, as shown in the Rage Damage column of the berserker table.
You have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to kinetic and energy damage.

entries: If you are able to cast powers, you can't cast them or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb}, you don {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}, or if your turn ends and you haven't taken a hostile action or taken damage since your last turn. You can also end your rage on your turn as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.
You can enter a rage a number of times as shown in the Rages column of the berserker table. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While you are not wearing any armor, your {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb} equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} and still gain this benefit.

classFeature.name: Reckless Attack
entries: You can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack rolls} using Strength during this turn, but {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} until your next turn.

classFeature.name: Berserker Instincts
entries: You've honed two instincts, as detailed at the end of the class description, and you hone more at higher levels, as shown in the Berserker Instincts column of the berserker table.

classFeature.name: Danger Sense
entries: You gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren't as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that you can see, such as traps and powers. To gain this benefit, you can't be {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded}, {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened}, or {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb}.

classFeature.name: Berserker Approach
entries: You choose an approach that shapes the nature of your rage which is detailed at the end of the class description.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Feral Impulse
entries: Your instincts are so honed that you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} checks.

Additionally, if you are surprised at the start of combat and aren't {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb}, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your rage before doing anything else on that turn.

classFeature.name: Brutal Critical
entries: You can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a melee attack.
This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

classFeature.name: Brutal Critical
entries: You can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a melee attack.
This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

classFeature.name: Brutal Critical
entries: You can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with a melee attack.
This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

classFeature.name: Relentless Rage
entries: Your rage can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} while you're raging and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead. Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, the DC resets to 10.

classFeature.name: Persistent Rage
entries: Your rage is so fierce that it ends early only if you fall {@condition Unconscious|sw5e-phb} or if you choose to end it.

classFeature.name: Indomitable Might
entries: If your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

classFeature.name: Primal Champion
entries: You embody the power of the wilds. Your Strength or Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 2. Your maximum for those scores increases by 2.
Additionally, you can enter rage an unlimited number of times, and entering rage no longer requires your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn.

classFeature.name: Berserker Instincts
entries: The instincts are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Acklay's Instinct
entries: While raging, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}.

entries.name: Bantha's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 7th level} Your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift doubles. If it would already double, it instead triples. Additionally, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Strength checks made to push, pull, lift, or break objects.

entries.name: Blurrg's Instinct
entries: Whether mounted or on foot, your travel pace is doubled, as is the travel pace of up to ten companions while they're within 60 feet of you and you're not {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Boggdo's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 13th level} While raging you have a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your current walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, though you fall if you end your turn in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft.

entries.name: Chirodactyl's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 7th level} While raging, you have blindsight to a range of 30 feet, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sound, as long as you aren't {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened}.

entries.name: Dewback's Instinct
entries: Choose three damage types other than true damage. While raging, you have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to the chosen damage types.

entries.name: Fighter's Instinct
entries: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the {@book Fighting Style options, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Fighting Styles}.

entries.name: Fyrnock's Instinct
entries: While raging, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to leap up to 30 feet to an empty space you can see. When you land you deal kinetic damage equal to your Strength modifier to each creature within 5 feet of where you land. You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Hawk's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 7th level} You can see up to 1 mile away with no difficulty. You are able to discern even fine details as though looking at something no more than 100 feet away from you. Additionally, dim light doesn't impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on your Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks.

entries.name: Katarn's Instinct
entries: You gain a climbing {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

entries.name: Loth-cat's Instinct
entries: While you're raging, other creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attack} rolls against you, and you can take the {@action Dash|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn.

entries.name: Predator's Instinct
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet.

entries.name: Rancor's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 13th level} While you're raging any creature within 5 feet of you that's hostile to you has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against targets other than you or another character with this feature. An enemy is immune to this effect if it can't see or hear you or if it can't be {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Tactician's Instinct
entries: When you use your Reckless Attack feature, you can choose to not have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} this turn. If you do so, friendly creatures within 5 feet of a hostile creature that is within 5 feet of you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature.

entries.name: Tracker's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 7th level} You can track other creatures while traveling at a fast pace, and you can move stealthily while traveling at a normal pace.

entries.name: Terentatek's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 13th level} When you are forced to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can immediately use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} towards the source power's caster. If you end this movement within 5 feet of the target, you can immediately make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against the target as a part of that {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Varactyl's Instinct
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 13th level} While raging, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity checks, your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} can't suffer from {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, and each {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level only reduces your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 5 feet, unless it would reduce your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} to 0.

classFeature.name: Berserker Approaches
entries: At 3rd level, you choose a berserker approache that you emulate. Your choice grants features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

classFeature.name: Berserker Approaches feature
entries: At 6th level, you gain a feature granted by your berserker approaches.

classFeature.name: Berserker Approaches feature
entries: At 10th level, you gain a feature granted by your berserker approaches.

classFeature.name: Berserker Approaches feature
entries: At 14th level, you gain a feature granted by your berserker approaches.

classFeature.name: Forcecasting
entries: In your meditations on the force, you have learned powers, fragments of knowledge that imbue you with an abiding force ability. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 11|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} for the {@book force powers list|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Force Powers Known
entries: You learn 9 {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Force Powers Known|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} column of the consular table. You may not learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level, and you may learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at the same time you learn its prerequisite.

entries.name: Force Points
entries: You have a number of force points equal to your consular level x 4, as shown in the Force Points column of the consular table, + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice). You use these force points to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. You regain all expended force points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} can be overpowered, consuming more force points to create a greater effect. You can overpower these abilities to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the consular table.
You may only cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Forcecasting Ability
entries: Your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} varies based on the alignment of the powers you cast. You use Wisdom for {@book light side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, Charisma for {@book dark side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and Wisdom or Charisma for {@book universal powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} (your choice). You use this ability whenever a power refers to your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Force save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier
{@b Force attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier

classFeature.name: Force Recovery
entries: You have learned to regain some of your energy by briefly meditating. When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you can regain a number of force points equal to half your consular level + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). Once you've used this feature, you must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

classFeature.name: Force-Empowered Casting
entries: You gain the ability to twist your powers to suit your needs. When you cast a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can expend additional force points to modify the power. You gain two Force-Empowered Casting options, located at the end of the class description, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the Force-Empowered Casting Options of the cnosular table.
You can use only one Force-Empowered Casting option on a power when you cast it, unless otherwise noted.

classFeature.name: Force Shield
entries: You learn how to defend yourself purely through your strength with the Force. When you are hit by an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to shroud yourself in Force energy. Until the start of your next turn, you have a bonus to AC equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1). This includes the triggering attack.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

classFeature.name: Force Affinity
entries: You've developed an affinity for one of the three aspects of the Force: the Ashla, the Bendu, or the Bogan. Choose one from the following:

entries.name: Ashla
entries: When you successfully cast a light side power, either your or the target's (your choice) hit point maximum and current {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} increase by an amount equal to the power's level. This effect lasts for 1 minute. You can only have one instance of this effect active at a time.

entries.name: Bendu
entries: You can add both your Wisdom and Charisma modifier to your maximum number of force points, instead of just one.

entries.name: Bogan
entries: Your dark side power damage rolls gain a minimum roll threshold, discussed in chapter 7.

classFeature.name: Consular Tradition
entries: You choose a consular tradition, which is detailed at the end of the class description.

classFeature.name: One with the Force
entries: Your attunement to the Force is absolute. Your Wisdom or Charisma score increases by 4, and your maximum for this score increases by 4. Additionally, you gain mastery over a single {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and can cast it with little effort. Choose one 3rd-level {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that you know as your signature power. You can cast it once at 3rd level without expending force points. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
If you want to cast it at a higher level, you must expend force points as normal.

classFeature.name: Force-Empowered Castings
entries: The castings are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Careful Power
entries: When you cast a power that forces other creatures to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can protect some of those creatures from the power's full force. To do so, you spend 1 additional force point and choose a number of those creatures up to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against the power.

entries.name: Distant Power
entries: When you cast a power that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 additional force point to double the range of the power.
Alternatively, when you cast a power that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 additional force point to make the range of the power 30 feet.

entries.name: Extended Power
entries: When you cast a power that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 additional force point to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

entries.name: Heightened Power
entries: When you cast a power that forces a creature to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist its effects, you can spend 3 additional force points to give one target of the power {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on its first {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} made against the power.

entries.name: Improved Power
entries: When you roll damage for a power, you can spend 1 additional force point to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one). You must use the new rolls.
You can use Improved Power even if you have already used a different Force-Empowered Casting option during the casting of the power.

entries.name: Lingering Power
entries: When you cast a power that requires {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} to maintain you can choose to spend 3 additional force points. If you do, when you lose {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on the power, the power will not end until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Pinpoint Power
entries: When you cast a power that allows you to force creatures in an area to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} you can instead spend 1 force point and make a ranged force attack against a single target that would be in the range. On a hit the target suffers the effects as though they failed their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Quickened Power
entries: When you cast a power that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 additional force points to change the casting time to 1 {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} for this casting.

entries.name: Refocused Power
entries: When you are forced to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to maintain {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on a power you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and spend 2 force points to automatically succeed on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.
You can use Refocused Power even if you have already used a different Force-Empowered Casting option during the casting of the power.

entries.name: Seeking Power
entries: If you miss with a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} that calls for an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can spend 2 force points to reroll the attack. You must use the new roll.
You can use Seeking Power even if you have already used a different Force-Empowered Casting option during the casting of the power.

entries.name: Twinned Power
entries: When you cast a power that can only have one target and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of additional force points equal to the power's level to choose a second target in range with the same power (1 force point if the power is at-will).

classFeature.name: Consular Traditions
entries: At 3rd level, you choose a consular tradition that you emulate. Your choice grants features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

classFeature.name: Consular Traditions feature
entries: At 6th level, you gain a feature granted by your consular traditions.

classFeature.name: Consular Traditions feature
entries: At 10th level, you gain a feature granted by your consular traditions.

classFeature.name: Consular Traditions feature
entries: At 14th level, you gain a feature granted by your consular traditions.

classFeature.name: Consular Traditions feature
entries: At 18th level, you gain a feature granted by your consular traditions.

classFeature.name: Techcasting
entries: During your training you have derived powers from schematics with the aid of your {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad}. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book techcasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 12|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} for the {@book tech powers list|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

entries.name: Tech Powers Known
entries: You learn 6 {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Tech Powers Known|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} column of the engineer table. You may not learn a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level.

entries.name: Tech Points
entries: You have a number of tech points equal to your engineer level x 2, as shown in the Tech Points column of the engineer table, + your Intelligence modifier. You use these tech points to cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You regain all expended tech points when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} can be overcharged, consuming more tech points to create a greater effect. You can overcharge these powers to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the engineer table.
You may only cast {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} at 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Techcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability} for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}. You use your Intelligence whenever a power refers to your {@book techcasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Techcasting Ability}. Additionally, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Tech save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier
{@b Tech attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Techcasting Focus
entries: You use a {@item Wristpad|sw5e-phb|wristpad} (found in {@book chapter 5|sw5e-phb|5}) or the tools in which you are granted proficiency by this class as a tech focus for your {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.

classFeature.name: Potent Aptitude
entries: Your technological experience lends you an uncommon insight that you can use to bolster your allies. To do so, you use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn to choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet of you who can hear you. That creature gains one Potent Aptitude die, a {@dice d4}. This die changes as you gain engineer levels, as shown in the Potent Aptitude column of the engineer table.

Once within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the number rolled to one {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} it makes. Once the Potent Aptitude die is rolled, it is lost.
A creature can have only one Potent Aptitude die at a time.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain any expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

classFeature.name: Infuse Item
entries: You gain the ability to temporarily enhance a weapon or armor. At the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can touch one unenhanced object that is a suit of armor, a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} or until you die, the object becomes an enhanced item, granting a +1 bonus to AC if it's armor or a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield} or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls if it's a weapon.
Once you've used this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
This bonus increases to +2 at 10th level and +3 at 15th level.

classFeature.name: Tool Expertise
entries: You gain {@variantrule Expertise|sw5e-phb|expertise} in any tool proficiencies you gain from this class.

classFeature.name: Tech Mastery
entries: Your mastery of technology is unrivaled. Your Constitution and Intelligence scores increase by 2. Your maximum for those scores increases by 2.
Additionally, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} and have no uses of Potent Aptitude left, you regain one use.

classFeature.name: Engineering Disciplines

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the {@book fighting style options, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Fighting Styles}.

classFeature.name: Second Wind
entries: You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to 1d10 + your fighter level.
Once you've used this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

classFeature.name: Action Surge
entries: You can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action.

Once you've used this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again. Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

classFeature.name: Combat Superiority
entries: You learn {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} that are fueled by special dice called {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. See {@book chapter 13|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} for the {@book maneuvers list|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}.

entries.name: Maneuvers Known
entries: You learn one {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} of your choice, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the Maneuvers Known column of the fighter table. Many {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} per attack, and you may only use each {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} once per turn.
Each time you learn new {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}, you can also replace one {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you know with a different one.

entries.name: Superiority Dice
entries: You have two {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}, which are d4s, and you earn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Quantity column of the fighter table. This die changes as you gain fighter levels, as shown in the {@book Superiority Dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} Size column of the fighter table. A superiority die is expended when you use it.
You regain all of your expended {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Maneuver Ability
entries: Your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} varies based on the type of the {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you use. You use Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution for {@book physical maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Physical} (your choice), Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma for {@book mental maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Mental} (your choice), and an ability of your choice for {@book general maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|General}. You use this ability whenever a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} refers to your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} you use.
{@b Maneuver save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book maneuver ability|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} modifier

classFeature.name: Fighter Strategies
entries: You've adopted a fighter strategy, as detailed at the end of the class description, and you adopt more at higher levels, as shown in the Strategies Known column of the fighter table.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Indomitable
entries: You can reroll a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.
You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level and three times between long rests starting at 17th level.

classFeature.name: Greater Extra Attack
entries: You can attack three times, instead of twice, whenever you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn.
Additionally, when you use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to engage in Double- or Two-Weapon Fighting, you can make two attacks, instead of one.

classFeature.name: Master of Combat
entries: You are the master of combat. Your Strength or Dexterity score increases by 2, and your Constitution score increases by 2. Your maximum for those scores increases by 2.
Additionally, you can attack four times, instead of three times, whenever you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Fighter Strategies
entries: The strategies are presented in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Cover Strategist
entries: You treat partial {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} as one step higher (from one-quarter to half or half to three-quarters). While in {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover}, your attacks reduce partial {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} by one step (from three-quarters to half or half to one-quarter).

entries.name: Cunning Strategist
entries: Choose two from the following. You can {@optfeature Perform|sw5e-phb|perform} each of the chosen options with your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, instead of your action:

items: Applying {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison}
Dash
Disengage
Guard
Help
Hide
Search
Throwing grenades and setting mines
While mounted on a controlled beast, having your beast make a single melee attack against a creature within its reach
While mounted on a vehicle, taking a vehicle action (you can't take the same action twice in one turn)

entries.name: Enduring Strategist
entries: You only need 3 hours of sleep during a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} to gain its benefits, instead of 6. Additionally, if your {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} would be interrupted, you only need to complete the {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} instead of restarting it to gain its benefits. Lastly, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.

entries.name: Mastery Strategist
entries: You've mastered a particular style of fighting. Choose one of the {@book Fighting Mastery options, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Fighting Masteries}.

entries.name: Lightweapon Strategist
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter all lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon}. Additionally, you no longer need the ability to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} to learn features that grant {@book lightsaber forms|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}, and you learn one {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms} of your choice.

entries.name: Maneuver Strategist
entries: You learn two additional {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}. When you complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, you can replace one of these {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} with another one. When you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can replace both of these {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} with other ones.

entries.name: Skilled Strategist
entries: You gain proficiency in a skill and a tool, or two tools.

entries.name: Style Strategist
entries: You adopt a second fighting style. Choose one of the {@book fighting style options, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Fighting Styles}. When you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can change this style out for another one.

classFeature.name: Fighter Specialties
entries: At 3rd level, you choose a fighter specialtie that you emulate. Your choice grants features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

classFeature.name: Fighter Specialties feature
entries: At 7th level, you gain a feature granted by your fighter specialties.

classFeature.name: Fighter Specialties feature
entries: At 10th level, you gain a feature granted by your fighter specialties.

classFeature.name: Fighter Specialties feature
entries: At 15th level, you gain a feature granted by your fighter specialties.

classFeature.name: Fighter Specialties feature
entries: At 18th level, you gain a feature granted by your fighter specialties.

classFeature.name: Forcecasting
entries: In your meditations on the Force, you have learned powers, fragments of knowledge that imbue you with an abiding force ability. See {@book chapter 10|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} for the general rules of {@book forcecasting|sw5e-phb|10|Force- and Tech-casting} and {@book chapter 11|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} for the {@book force powers list|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

entries.name: Force Powers Known
entries: You learn 5 {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of your choice, and you learn more at higher levels, as shown in the {@book Force Powers Known|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} column of the guardian table. You may not learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} of a level higher than your Max Power Level, and you may learn a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at the same time you learn its prerequisite.

entries.name: Force Points
entries: You have a number of force points equal to your guardian level x 2, as shown in the Force Points column of the guardian table, + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice). You use these force points to cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}. You regain all expended force points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Max Power Level
entries: Many {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} can be overpowered, consuming more force points to create a greater effect. You can overpower these abilities to a maximum level, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Max Power Level column of the guardian table.
You may only cast {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} at 4th and 5th-level once. You regain the ability to do so after a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Forcecasting Ability
entries: Your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} varies based on the alignment of the powers you cast. You use Wisdom for {@book light side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, Charisma for {@book dark side powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, and Wisdom or Charisma for {@book universal powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} (your choice). You use this ability whenever a power refers to your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability}. Additionally, you use this ability modifier when setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for a {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} you cast and when making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with one.
{@b Force save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier
{@b Force attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} modifier

classFeature.name: Channel the Force
entries: You know how to channel the Force to create a unique effect. You start with your choice of one from two such effects: Cause Harm or Lend Aid. At 3rd level, your Guardian Focus grants you an additional effect. When you use your Channel the Force, you choose which effect to create.
Some Channel the Force effects require {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your universal force save DC.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: Cause Harm
entries: As an action, you can expend a use of your Channel the Force to sap the life from a hostile creature you can see within 60 feet. That creature must make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, the creature takes necrotic damage equal to your guardian level + your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1), or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Lend Aid
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can expend a use of your Channel the Force and touch a beast or humanoid within 5 feet of you. That creature regains {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your guardian level + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1). Alternatively, if the beast or humanoid is {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb} or {@condition Diseased|sw5e-phb|diseased}, you neutralize the {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} or disease. If more than one {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} or disease afflicts the target, you neutralize one {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} or disease that you know is present, or you neutralize one at random.

classFeature.name: Force-Empowered Strikes
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, you can expend force points to deal additional damage to the target, which is the same type as the weapon's damage. The additional damage is 1d8 for each point spent in this way. You can't deal more additional damage than the amount shown in the Focused Strikes column of the guardian table.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the {@book fighting style options, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Fighting Styles}.

classFeature.name: Guardian Aura
entries: You gain an aura of your choice, as detailed at the end of the class description, and you gain more at higher levels, as shown in the Auras Known column of the guardian table. Your aura has a radius of 5 feet, which increases at higher levels, as shown in the Aura Radius column of the guardian table.

classFeature.name: Guardian Focus
entries: You begin to focus your studies on a specific {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}, which is detailed at the end of the class description.

classFeature.name: Guardian Focus
entries: You begin to focus your studies on a specific {@book lightsaber form|sw5e-phb|6|Lightsaber Forms}, which is detailed at the end of the class description.

classFeature.name: Guardian Focus

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You can increase one ability score by 2, or you can increase two ability scores by 1. You can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Force Purity
entries: The Force flowing through you makes you immune to {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} and disease.

classFeature.name: Improved Force-Empowered Strikes
entries: You are so in tune with the Force that all your melee weapon strikes carry the power of the Force with them. Whenever you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack}, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage. The damage is the same type as the weapon's damage.

classFeature.name: Cleansing Touch
entries: You can use your action and expend a use of your Channel the Force ability to end one {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} on yourself or on one willing creature that you touch.

classFeature.name: Guardian Auras
entries: The auras are presented in alphabetical order. If multiple guardians grant the same aura, affected creatures can only benefit from it once. You must be conscious to grant the benefits of your auras.

entries.name: Aura of Conquest
entries: Whenever a creature who is {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb} of you starts its turn within 5 feet of you, its gains 4 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} levels and takes psychic damage equal to half your guardian level.

entries.name: Aura of Conviction
entries: You and friendly creatures within 5 feet of you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against effects that would cause you to be {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Aura of Hatred
entries: You and friendly creatures within 5 feet of you gain a bonus to the first melee weapon damage rolls you make each round equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1).

entries.name: Aura of Presence
entries: Whenever you or a friendly creature within 5 feet of you must make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, the creature can add your Wisdom modifier to the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}.

entries.name: Aura of Protection
entries: Whenever a creature within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to take that damage instead of that creature taking it. This feature doesn't transfer any other effects that might accompany the damage, and this damage can't be reduced in any way.

entries.name: Aura of Vigor
entries: Whenever a friendly creature starts its turn within 5 feet of you, that creature gains temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of one).

entries.name: Aura of Warding
entries: You and friendly creatures within 5 feet of you have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to damage from {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}.

classFeature.name: Guardian Foci
entries: At 3rd level, you choose a guardian foci that you emulate. Your choice grants features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

classFeature.name: Guardian Foci feature
entries: At 7th level, you gain a feature granted by your guardian foci.

classFeature.name: Guardian Foci feature
entries: At 15th level, you gain a feature granted by your guardian foci.

classFeature.name: Guardian Foci feature
entries: At 20th level, you gain a feature granted by your guardian foci.

classFeature.name: Martial Arts
entries: Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and monk weapons, which are {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon} with which you are proficient that lack the dexterity, heavy, special, and two-handed properties.
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only monk weapons and you aren't wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}:

items: Your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes} and monk weapons gain {@itemProperty SWF|sw5e-phb|the finesse property}.
You can roll a {@dice d4} in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or monk weapon. This die changes as you gain monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the monk table.
You can use Dexterity instead of Strength whenever you would make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|sw5e-phb}) check to grapple, shove, or trip a creature.
When you use the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action with an unarmed strike or a monk weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.
You can take the Dash or Disengage actions as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

entries.name: Variant: Monks with Lightweapons
entries: If monks gain {@filter lightweapon|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} proficiency, consider letting them use {@filter lightweapons|items|type=martial weapon|category=lightweapon} as monk weapons, provided the weapon lacks the dexterity, heavy, special, and two-handed properties.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: While you are wearing no armor and not wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}, your AC equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice).

classFeature.name: Focus
entries: Your training allows you to harness the mystic energy of focus. Your access to this energy is represented by a number of focus points. Your monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Focus Points column of the monk table.

You can spend these points to fuel various focus features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more focus features as you gain levels in this class.

When you spend a focus point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, at the end of which you draw all of your expended focus back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your focus points.

You use your choice of Wisdom or Charisma for your focus ability. You use the chosen ability modifier whenever a feature refers to your focus ability. Additionally, you use the chosen ability modifier when making an attack with a focus feature or setting the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC for one.
{@b Focus save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice)
{@b Focus attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice)

entries.name: Flurry of Blows
entries: When you make your Martial Arts {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} attack, you can spend 1 focus point to make an additional unarmed strike (no action required). At 11th level, you can instead spend 2 focus points to make two additional {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|sw5e-phb|unarmed strikes}.

entries.name: Patient Defense
entries: When you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to Disengage, you can spend 1 focus point to also Dodge (no action required). At 11th level, you can instead spend 2 focus points to Dodge and gain an additional {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Step of the Wind
entries: When you use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to Dash, you can spend 1 focus point to double your jump distance for the turn. At 11th level, you can instead spend 2 focus points to gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} until the end of your turn, though you fall if you end your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft.

You can spend these points to fuel various focus features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind. You learn more focus features as you gain levels in this class.

When you spend a focus point, it is unavailable until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, at the end of which you draw all of your expended focus back into yourself. You must spend at least 30 minutes of the rest meditating to regain your focus points.

You use your choice of Wisdom or Charisma for your focus ability. You use the chosen ability modifier whenever a feature refers to your focus ability. {@b Focus attack modifier} = your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice)

At 11th level, you can instead spend 2 focus points to gain a flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} equal to your walking {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} until the end of your turn, though you fall if you end your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} in the air and nothing else is holding you aloft.

classFeature.name: Monastic Vows
entries: You've sworn two vows, as detailed at the end of the class description. You swear an additional vow at 7th, 13th, and 17th level.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Movement
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in the Unarmored Movement column of the monk table.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

classFeature.name: Unarmored Movement
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|sw5e-phb|shield}. This bonus increases when you reach certain monk levels, as shown in the Unarmored Movement column of the monk table.
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.

classFeature.name: Deflect Missiles
entries: You can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to deflect a projectile when you are dealt damage by a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}. When you do so, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + your Dexterity modifier + your monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, and the damage is kinetic, energy, or ion, you can redirect it at another target if you have a weapon capable of doing so. You can spend 1 focus point to make a ranged attack with a range of 20/60 as you deflect the projectile, as part of the same {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}. You make this attack with proficiency, regardless of your weapon proficiencies, and the projectile counts as a monk weapon for the attack.

classFeature.name: Monastic Order
entries: You commit yourself to one monastic order, which is detailed at the end of the class description.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
