On a failed save, the next time you would make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the target before the end of your next turn, you can instead force the target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} with the ability score of your choice. On a failed save, the creature takes normal weapon damage, is subjected to any additional effects that would occur on a hit, and you can apply your Sneak Attack damage to the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Infiltrator
entries: You have become a master at avoiding detection.

When you or a creature within 5 feet of you fails a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) check, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to allow that creature to reroll the check. It must use the new roll.

subclassFeature.name: Bushmaster
entries: You excel at leading ambushes and acting first in a fight.

You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} checks. Additionally, the first creature you hit during the first round of a combat becomes easier for you and others to strike; {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that target have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Death Strike
entries: You've become a master of instant death. When you deal weapon damage to a creature that you are hidden from or that is surprised, you can force it to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your lethal strike save DC. On a failed save, double the damage of your attack against the creature, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Sharpshooter Practice
entries: Those operatives who choose the Sharpshooter Practice are bringers of death. Striking from a safe distance, the Sharpshooter uses precision shooting to control the battlefield and bring targets down quickly.

subclassFeature.name: Assume the Position
entries: You don't need {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} to use your Sneak Attack if your target is greater than 30 feet from you and no enemies are within 5 feet of you. Additionally, standing up from prone now only costs 5 feet of movement.
Additionally, you gain proficiency with two martial {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Placed Shots
entries: You perfect the art of placing distant shots for maximum effectiveness in debilitating and controlling your enemies. When you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you may choose to forgo two of your Sneak Attack dice to make the attack a placed shot.

Some of your placed shots require your target to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the placed shot's effects. The {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} DC is calculated as follows:
{@b Placed Shot save DC} = 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Dexterity modifier

entries.name: Disarming Shot
entries: You attempt to disarm a creature with your attack. The target must succeed on a Strength {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be forced to drop one item of your choice that it's holding. The object lands at its feet.

entries.name: Penetrating Shot
entries: You attempt to damage another target with the same attack. Choose a second target within 15 feet of and directly behind your initial target. If the original {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} would hit the second target, it takes two dice worth of Sneak Attack damage.
The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.

entries.name: Suppressive Shot
entries: You attempt to pin the target to its location. The target must succeed on a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} or be {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb} of you until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Head Shot
entries: You are at your deadliest when your enemies are unaware of the danger they are in. You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against any creature that hasn't taken a turn in combat yet.
Additionally, any hit you score against a creature that is surprised is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}.

subclassFeature.name: Distracting Shot
entries: You are able to defend your compatriots from afar. When a friendly creature you can see within your weapon's normal range is the target of a ranged attack, or forced to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and the source of the effect is within your weapon's normal range, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against the source. On a hit, instead of dealing damage, the target of your attack has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against your ally, or your ally has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to resist the effect.

subclassFeature.name: Double Tap
entries: You've learned to capitalize when you have the {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action and make an attack with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, you can choose to forgo the {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. If you do, you can make an additional attack against the target or another creature within 5 feet of it (no action required). Both attacks can benefit from your Sneak Attack damage, instead of only one.

subclassFeature.name: Gambler Pursuit
entries: Not all studied men and women use their intelligence and skill for the pursuit of knowledge, but instead turn to the various casinos and betting halls of the galaxy. Those scholars who choose the Gambler Pursuit use their knowledge of probability and risk to attempt to master games of chance and build their fortune, or lose it all along the way.

subclassFeature.name: Gambler's Aptitude
entries: You gain proficiency with your choice of gaming set and your choice of the {@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}, or Sleight of Hand skills. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

subclassFeature.name: Risk versus Reward
entries: When you make your first attack on your turn against the target of your Critical Analysis feature, you can decide to gamble by rolling a {@dice d6}. On a roll of 4 or higher, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature until the start of your next turn. On a roll of 3 or lower, that creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you until the start of your next turn.
This die increases to {@dice d8} at 9th level, {@dice d10} at 13th level, and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Risk versus Reward
entries: When you make your first attack on your turn against the target of your Critical Analysis feature, you can decide to gamble by rolling a {@dice d6}. On a roll of 4 or higher, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature until the start of your next turn. On a roll of 3 or lower, that creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you until the start of your next turn.
This die increases to {@dice d8} at 9th level, {@dice d10} at 13th level, and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Risk versus Reward
entries: When you make your first attack on your turn against the target of your Critical Analysis feature, you can decide to gamble by rolling a {@dice d6}. On a roll of 4 or higher, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature until the start of your next turn. On a roll of 3 or lower, that creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you until the start of your next turn.
This die increases to {@dice d8} at 9th level, {@dice d10} at 13th level, and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Risk versus Reward
entries: When you make your first attack on your turn against the target of your Critical Analysis feature, you can decide to gamble by rolling a {@dice d6}. On a roll of 4 or higher, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against that creature until the start of your next turn. On a roll of 3 or lower, that creature instead has {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} against you until the start of your next turn.
This die increases to {@dice d8} at 9th level, {@dice d10} at 13th level, and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Lucky Number 7
entries: Whenever you roll a 7 on an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against the target of your Critical Analysis feature, the attack automatically hits and you regain an expended superiority die.

When attacking with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, this effect applies if either roll is a 7. If both rolls are a 7, the attack is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}.

subclassFeature.name: Tell Me the Odds
entries: If the target of your Critical Analysis hits you with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} roll, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to roll a {@dice d8}. On a 4 or higher, you impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the roll. If the target already had {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, they must instead reroll one of the dice once (your choice).
This die increases to {@dice d10} at 13th level and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Tell Me the Odds
entries: If the target of your Critical Analysis hits you with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} roll, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to roll a {@dice d8}. On a 4 or higher, you impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the roll. If the target already had {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, they must instead reroll one of the dice once (your choice).
This die increases to {@dice d10} at 13th level and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Tell Me the Odds
entries: If the target of your Critical Analysis hits you with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} roll, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to roll a {@dice d8}. On a 4 or higher, you impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the roll. If the target already had {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, they must instead reroll one of the dice once (your choice).
This die increases to {@dice d10} at 13th level and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Borrowed Luck
entries: You have gained the ability to unnaturally alter luck in your favor. Once per round, after an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, or {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} is rolled by you or a creature that you can see, you can replace the number on the {@dice d20} with a 7. Note the number on the {@dice d20} of the roll that you replaced. That number becomes your borrowed luck roll.

While you have a borrowed luck roll, you can expend it and replace any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check}, {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} made by you or a creature that you can see with the value of the borrowed luck roll. You can only have one borrowed luck roll at a time, and you lose any unused borrowed luck rolls when you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Gambler Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your deep understanding of chance. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Ace Up Your Sleeve
entries: Whenever you make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) or Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check, you can expend a superiority die, adding the result to your total for the check.

entries.name: Against the House
entries: Whenever you would make a Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) check involving haggling, you can instead challenge the target to a game of chance. If they accept your offer, you can make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} with an available gaming set. If you win the challenge, you automatically succeed on the Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) check.

entries.name: Ante Up
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative}, are not surprised, and end up first in the {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} order, you can take one additional action on top of your regular action and a possible {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} during your first turn in combat.

entries.name: Calculated Bluff
entries: When you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} using Charisma, you can choose to instead make the check using your Intelligence or Wisdom modifier (your choice).

entries.name: Cold Read
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} As an action, you may make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|sw5e-phb}) check contested by a target's Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}) check. On a success, you know the next action the target intends to take, so long as the situation does not change dramatically.

entries.name: Feeling the Pressure
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 13th level} Whenever you roll a 4 or higher on your Risk Versus Reward feature, the target of your Critical Analysis feature also has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} made against you until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Take a Chance
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} Before making an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}, you can expend a superiority die. On a miss, you lose that superiority die and do not benefit from it in any way. On a hit, you can choose two other {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} that you know, and subject the target to both {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}, without expending additional {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers}.

entries.name: The Magic Number
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 7th level} Whenever you roll a 7 on an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can reroll the {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

subclassFeature.name: Physician Pursuit
entries: Physicians study the medical, anatomical, and biological sciences. Those scholars who choose the Physician Pursuit use their knowledge to mend their allies on the field and deal crippling blows with surgical precision.

subclassFeature.name: Medical Practitioner
entries: You gain proficiency with biochemist's kits and your choice of the {@skill Medicine|sw5e-phb} or {@skill Nature|sw5e-phb} skills. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with them.

subclassFeature.name: Remote Healer
entries: You have learned to deploy medicine from a range. When you use a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} targeting an ally that is the target of your Critical Analysis feature, that {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers}'s range becomes 30 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Field Surgeon
entries: Whenever you expend {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to a creature, you can roll an additional {@dice d6} and add it to the roll. This die increases to {@dice d8} at 9th level, {@dice d10} at 13th level, and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

Additionally, whenever you expend {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to a creature, if the creature is the target of your Critical Analysis, you can instead choose the maximum on both dice. Once you've used this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again. Starting at 11th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

subclassFeature.name: Field Surgeon
entries: Whenever you expend {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to a creature, you can roll an additional {@dice d6} and add it to the roll. This die increases to {@dice d8} at 9th level, {@dice d10} at 13th level, and {@dice d12} at 17th level.

Additionally, whenever you expend {@book superiority dice|sw5e-phb|13|Superiority and Maneuvers} to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or grant temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to a creature, if the creature is the target of your Critical Analysis, you can instead choose the maximum on both dice. Once you've used this feature, you must finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again. Starting at 11th level, you can use it twice before a rest, but only once on the same turn.

subclassFeature.name: Resuscitate
entries: Through your medical studies you have learned to delay seemingly inevitable death. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can stabilize a creature you can touch that has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.

Additionally, as an action, you can tend to a creature you can touch that has died since the end of your last turn. The creature immediately regains 1 hit point and stabilizes. Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Panacea
entries: You've developed the formula to concoct a cure-all miracle solution: a panacea. Over the course of 10 minutes, you can expend rare medical supplies worth 1,000 cr to create your panacea in a simple syringe. The panacea retains its potency for 24 hours. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, a creature can use the panacea. Alternatively, as an action, they can administer it to another creature within 5 feet.

The target has its {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion} level reduced by one and regains all of its {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. If the target is {@condition Diseased|sw5e-phb|diseased}, {@condition Poisoned|sw5e-phb}, {@condition Paralyzed|sw5e-phb|paralyzed}, or {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned}, the condition ends.
Once you create a panacea, you can't create another until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Physician Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect the progress of your studies into the medical arts. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Advanced Remote Healer
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 11th level} The range of your Remote {@feat Healer|sw5e-phb} feature increases to 60 feet.

entries.name: Experimental Treatments
entries: Your medication and treatments are known to be untested and unstable. Immediately after you use a {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} that causes a creature to regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} or gain temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you can choose to roll on the Side Effects table to the right. The condition or effect lasts until the creature completes a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, or you use this feature again.
You can use this feature twice. You gain an additional use at 5th, 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

entries.name: From the Brink
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 7th level} If the target of your Critical Analysis feature would be reduced to 0 hp, you may use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and end your Critical Analysis feature to have them be reduced to 1 hp instead. Once a creature has benefited from this feature, they must complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before they can do so again.

entries.name: Health Advisor
entries: Whenever a creature that is a target of your Critical Analysis feature begins their turn, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to give them temporary {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to one-fourth your scholar level + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}, as shown in the scholar table, which last until the start of their next turn.

entries.name: Patient Protector
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} You can treat creatures within 5 feet of the target of your Critical Analysis feature as if they were also targets of your Critical Analysis.

entries.name: Surgical Precision
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} When you hit a creature that is the target of your Critical Analysis feature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, it takes additional damage equal to your Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Tend the Wounded
entries: If you or any friendly creatures you can touch regain {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} by spending one or more Hit Dice at the end of a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}, each of those creatures regain 1d4 extra {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}.
This die increases when you reach certain levels in this class: 1d6 at 5th level, 1d8 at 9th level, 1d10 at 13th level, and to 1d12 at 17th level.

rows: The creature turns out to be allergic to this specific treatment. Every ability score is reduced by 1.
The creature starts sneezing uncontrollably. Any {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} with a die roll value of 19 results in a miss due to a poorly timed sneeze.
The creature's legs become swollen. The creature gains 1 {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed} level.
The creature becomes one size larger or smaller.
The skin at their joints turns into a wooden material, giving them a bonus of +2 to AC.

The creature's body starts producing powerful stomach acid in high amounts. The creature can use an action to spew stomach acid in a 15 feet cone. The DC for this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} + your Constitution modifier. A creature takes 2d6 acid damage on a failed save, and half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to 3d6 at 5th level, 4d6 at 11th level, and 5d6 at 17th level.
The creature becomes mute and has uncontrollable gas. They have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on smell.

The creature's eyes glows bright red. The creature also gains {@spell Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision}, but if they already have {@spell Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision} they get a light headache instead.
The creature gains {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on perception checks based on hearing, but everything seems uncomfortably loud to them. They gain vulnerability to sonic damage.
The treatment slows down their brain function, reducing their Intelligence by 4.
The creature's skin turns dark purple. If they are already purple, they turn bright pink instead.
The creature becomes covered in sickly, green pustules. When the creature is hit by a melee attack, the attacker takes 1d4 {@item Poison|sw5e-phb|poison} damage.

The creature's skin starts to seriously bloat up from internal pressure build-up, and a strong impact may cause it to explode. Whenever the creature takes damage, the creature has to pass a {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} check or the creature takes kinetic damage equal to half their maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}. Other creatures within 10 feet of the {@spell Explosion|sw5e-phb|explosion} also take a fourth of the damage. Once this {@spell Explosion|sw5e-phb|explosion} occurs, their skin becomes very soft.

The creature rapidly grows body hair all over, including the face, until they resemble a wookiee. If they are already a wookiee, the reverse effect occurs; all hair immediately falls off, leaving the skin bare.
The creature's body temperature fluctuates to extremes. They gain {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to cold and fire damage.
The creature becomes ravenous. Every hour they haven't eaten a meal they gain a level of {@condition Exhaustion|sw5e-phb|exhaustion}.
The creature believes they are the chosen one.
The creature has a difficult time resting. The amount they heal from Hit Dice is now halved.

The creature's movement {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is increased by 15 feet, and {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} on them have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.
The creature gains 10d10 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, and they feel happy and carefree.

subclassFeature.name: Politician Pursuit
entries: Politicians study social & political sciences. Those scholars who choose the Politician Pursuit know how to best present themselves to manipulate the masses into doing their bidding or allow them and their allies to carry out their business without impediment. They also understand the importance of {@optfeature Self-Preservation|sw5e-phb|self-preservation} for a political figure.

subclassFeature.name: Silver Tongue
entries: You learn your choice of two languages and your choice of Charisma skill. Additionally, you can't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on checks you make with it.

subclassFeature.name: Motivating Diplomat
entries: When you are the target of your Critical Analysis feature, you and all allies within 10 feet of you gain a bonus to their AC equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Force of Personality
entries: As an action, you suggest a course of activity (limited to a sentence or two) to influence a creature you can see within range that can hear and understand you. Creatures that can't be {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} are immune to this effect. The suggestion must be worded in such a manner as to make the course of action sound reasonable. Asking the creature to stab itself, throw itself onto a spear, {@spell Immolate|sw5e-phb|immolate} itself, or do some other obviously harmful act ends the effect.

The target must make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} save DC. On a failed save, the target is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by you, and it pursues the course of action you described to the best of its ability. The suggested course of action can continue for up to 24 hours. If the suggested activity can be completed in a shorter time, the effect ends when the subject finishes what it was asked to do.

You can also specify conditions that will trigger a special activity during the duration. For example, you might suggest that an officer givers her gun to the first smuggler she meets. If the condition isn't met before the effect ends, the activity isn't performed.
If you or any of your companions damage the target, the effect ends.
You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Reassemble
entries: You may use to a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to call your allies towards you. When you do so, choose a number of creatures that you can see within 60 feet of you equal to your Critical Analysis ability modifier (minimum of one). They can use their {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to immediately move a number of feet equal to their {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. This movement does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}, and they must end this movement closer to you than they started.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Beguiling Presence
entries: Humanoids within 60 feet are particularly susceptible to your presence. Humanoids within range have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against any charm or fear effects that originate from you.

subclassFeature.name: Politician Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect the progress of your studies into the political world. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Charming Feint
entries: Allies within range of your Motivating Diplomat feature also gain a bonus to their damage rolls equal to half your Critical Analysis ability modifier.

entries.name: Demanding Leader
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} The range of each of your {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} increases by 10 feet. If the range is touch, it becomes 10 feet.

entries.name: Dominating Presence
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 15th level} As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, you can call out to a humanoid who can understand you that is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by you or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb} of you to direct their next action. The target must succeed a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} save DC. On a failed save, until the end of your next turn, the creature takes only the actions you choose, and doesn't do anything that you don't allow it to do.
During this time you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to force the creature to use its {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb}.
Once you've used this feature, you must complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Influencer
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} The range on the your Motivating Diplomat feature is increased to 15 feet.

entries.name: Reliable Words
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} Charisma ({@skill Deception|sw5e-phb}, {@skill Intimidation|sw5e-phb}, or {@skill Persuasion|sw5e-phb}) checks you make gain a minimum roll threshold, discussed in chapter 7.

entries.name: Social Opportunist
entries: You can add half your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} to any Charisma check you make that doesn't already include your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Tyrant's Ferocity
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on any attack against a creature that is {@condition Charmed|sw5e-phb|charmed} by you or {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb} of you.

subclassFeature.name: Tactician Pursuit
entries: Tacticians study strategy and the ways of war. Those scholars who choose the Tactician Pursuit train themselves and their allies in combat {@book maneuvers|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} to deftly eliminate their foes through clever positioning, and fierce, timely attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Battle Display
entries: You gain proficiency in martial {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} and martial {@filter vibroweapons|items|type=martial weapon}.

subclassFeature.name: Tactical Mastery
entries: You learn to better command your allies to victory from afar. Your Critical Analysis range is increased to 90 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Fire as One
entries: You can focus your target down with the help with an ally. Once per round, whenever the creature that is the target of your Critical Analysis feature is attacked by someone other than you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against them.

subclassFeature.name: Battlefield Survey
entries: You become a master at leading your allies around in a battlefield you have studied. When you spend 10 minutes observing an area that is within 120 feet from you, or by using a detailed map, select a number of creatures up to your Critical Analysis ability modifier. You and those selected allies ignore unenhanced {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain}, and have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) checks in that area.

subclassFeature.name: All-Out Attack
entries: You can use your action to initiate an all-out attack. Choose a number of allies up to your Critical Analysis ability modifier within 60 feet who can see or hear you. The chosen allies may then immediately use their {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against a target of your choice. You may choose the target for each attack separately.
Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Tactician Discoveries
entries: When you select this pursuit, you gain access to new discoveries which reflect your mastery in the field of combat. Whenever you learn a new discovery, you can choose from any of the following as well. The discoveries are listed in alphabetical order.

entries.name: Commander's Armor
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 5th level} You gain proficiency in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}. If you are already proficient in {@filter medium armor|items|type=medium armor}, you instead gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

entries.name: Contingency Plan
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 9th level} When the target of your Critical Analysis feature scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and expend a superiority die to treat the attack as a normal hit instead.

entries.name: Fighting Style
entries: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the {@book fighting style options, detailed in chapter 6|sw5e-phb|6|Fighting Styles}.

entries.name: Firing Command
entries: You can take the {@action Help|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}. Additionally, when you take the {@action Help|sw5e-phb} action to {@optfeature Assist|sw5e-phb|assist} an ally attacking the target of your Critical Analysis, it has a range of 30 feet.

entries.name: Observant Leader
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) checks that rely on sight.

entries.name: Studied Commander
entries: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Lore|sw5e-phb}) or Intelligence ({@skill Technology|sw5e-phb}) check related to battles, tactics, or weaponry, you may expend a superiority die and add it to the roll.

entries.name: Tactical Retreat
entries: When you take the {@action Dash|sw5e-phb} action, {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks} made against you are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Unbound Commander
entries: {@i {@b Prerequisite:} 12th level} You learn to command your allies to victory from afar. Your Critical Analysis range is increased to 120 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Bulwark Technique
entries: Some scouts find themselves far from civilization not to hunt, gather intelligence, or escape danger, but to venture forth simply to defend those unable to defend themselves. Followers of the Bulwark Technique make use of advanced technology to contain those that {@optfeature Threaten|sw5e-phb|threaten} the undeserving.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

subclassFeature.name: Personal Barrier
entries: You gain access to a powerful personal barrier. Whenever you complete a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you create a barrier on yourself that lasts until you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}. That barrier has {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to twice your scout level + your Intelligence modifier. Your barrier can never have {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} greater than twice your scout level + your Intelligence modifier.
Whenever you take damage, the barrier takes the damage instead. If this damage reduces the barrier to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you take any remaining damage.

While the barrier has 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, it can't absorb damage, but its power remains. Whenever you cast a {@book tech power|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers} of 1st level or higher, your barrier regains {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to the number of tech points spent.
Additionally, for as long as your barrier has {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, you gain the following benefits:

items: You are considered proficient in Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} for the purpose of maintaining {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} on {@book tech powers|sw5e-phb|12|Tech Powers}.
Hostile creatures that hit you with melee attacks take energy damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one).

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Bulwark
entries: When the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature makes a melee attack against a friendly creature within 5 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to force the attack to target you instead. If the attack hits, and your Personal Barrier has {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points}, the attacking creature takes bonus damage equal to your Ranger's Quarry Damage Die.

subclassFeature.name: Projected Barrier
entries: You've learned how to manipulate your barrier to create new effects. As an action, you can spend three of your barrier's {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} to create a unique effect. You have three such effects: Projected Sphere, Projected Maelstrom, and Projected Wave. When you use your Projected Barrier, you choose which effect to create.
Some Projected Barrier Effects require {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. When you use such an effect from this class, the DC equals your tech save DC.
If your barrier's {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} are reduced to 0, any Projected Barrier features immediately end.

entries.name: Projected Sphere
entries: You create a protective spherical barrier in a 5-foot-radius sphere a point you can see within 30 feet that lasts until the start of your next turn. Creatures within the barrier have three-quarters {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-phb|cover} from attacks originating from outside the barrier. You can maintain the barrier by spending an additional barrier hit point at the start of each of your turns (no action required).

entries.name: Projected Maelstrom
entries: You create an unstable energy maelstrom in a 5-foot cube at a point you can see within 30 feet that lasts until the start of your next turn. A creature takes 4d4 energy damage when it enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there. You can maintain the barrier by spending an additional barrier hit point at the start of each of your turns (no action required).
This feature's damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 11th level (5d4) and 17th level (6d4).

entries.name: Projected Wave
entries: You create a wave of barrier energy in a 15-foot cone. Each creature within the cone must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d6 energy damage and is pushed back to the edge of the cone. On a success, they take half damage and aren't pushed.
This feature's damage increases by 1d6 when you reach 11th level (3d6) and 17th level (4d6).

subclassFeature.name: Regenerative Shielding
entries: When a hostile creature forces you to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} and you succeed, your personal barrier regains {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} equal to your Intelligence modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Adaptive Barrier
entries: When your personal barrier takes damage, you can have it gain {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to subsequent damage of that type until the start of your next turn (no action required). If it takes damage of more than one type simultaneously, you can choose which type it gains {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to. Your barrier can only have {@spell Resistance|sw5e-phb|resistance} to one type of damage at a time.

subclassFeature.name: Hunter Technique
entries: Some scouts seek to master weapons to better protect civilization from the terrors of their enemies. Followers of the Hunter Technique learn specialized fighting techniques for use against the most dire threats, from an onslaught of soldiers to towering walkers.

subclassFeature.name: Hunter's Prey
entries: You gain one of the following features of your choice.

entries.name: Colossus Slayer
entries: Your {@optfeature Tenacity|sw5e-phb|tenacity} can wear down the most potent foes. When you hit a creature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, the creature takes an extra 1d8 damage if it's below its hit point maximum. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn, and this damage is the same type as the weapon's damage.

entries.name: Giant Killer
entries: When a Large or larger creature within 5 feet of you hits or misses you with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to attack that creature immediately after its attack, provided that you can see the creature.

entries.name: Horde Breaker
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack}, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within range of your weapon, no action required.

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Hunter
entries: When you use your Ranger's Quarry feature, the first time you make a tech or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against the target of your Ranger's Quarry each turn, roll your Ranger's Quarry die and add it to the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Defensive Tactics
entries: You gain one of the following features of your choice.

entries.name: Escape the Horde
entries: Opportunity attacks against you are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Multiattack Defense
entries: When a creature hits you with an attack, you gain a +4 bonus to AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.

entries.name: Steel Will
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against being {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Multiattack
entries: You gain one of the following features of your choice.

entries.name: Volley
entries: You can use your action to make a ranged attack against any number of creatures within 10 feet of a point you can see within your weapon's range. You must have ammunition for each target, as normal, and you make a separate {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} for each target.

entries.name: Whirlwind Attack
entries: You can use your action to make melee attacks against any number of creatures within 5 feet of you, with a separate {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} for each target.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Hunter's Defense
entries: You gain one of the following features of your choice.

entries.name: Evasion
entries: When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, and only half damage if you fail.

entries.name: Stand Against the Tide
entries: When a hostile creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to force that creature to repeat the same attack against another creature (other than itself) of your choice.

entries.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to halve the attack's damage against you.

subclassFeature.name: Slayer Technique
entries: Some scouts seek to learn the most about their foes and to capitalize on that knowledge. Followers of the Slayer Technique focus on identifying the strengths and weaknesses of their prey, taking {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} of that knowledge to vanquish their foes.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency in {@filter heavy armor|items|type=heavy armor}.

subclassFeature.name: Slayer's Pride
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws} against being {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Slayer
entries: You immediately learn if the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature has any damage immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities and what they are. Additionally, the first time you hit the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature with a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} each turn, it takes extra damage equal to your Ranger's Quarry Damage Die. The damage is of the same type as the weapon's damage.

subclassFeature.name: Supernatural Defense
entries: Whenever the target of your Ranger's Quarry forces you to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, or whenever you make an {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} to escape that targets grapple, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} and roll your Ranger's Quarry Damage Die, adding it to the roll.

subclassFeature.name: Nemesis
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} or reduce a creature to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|sw5e-phb|hit points} on your turn, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to force one creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, a creature becomes {@condition Frightened|sw5e-phb} of you for 1 minute. At the end of each of the creature's turns it repeats this {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, ending the effect on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Slayer's Counter
entries: If the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature forces you to make a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to make one {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against it. You make this attack immediately before making the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}. If your attack hits, you automatically succeed on the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}, in addition to the attack's normal effects.

subclassFeature.name: Stalker Technique
entries: Some Scouts become consumed by the thrill of the hunt. Only heard and never seen they revel in the violence of battle. Followers of the Stalker Technique hone their abilities to track others utilizing a variety of techniques: camouflage, infiltration, surveillance, and target acquisition.

subclassFeature.name: Accomplished Ambusher
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action against a creature that is surprised, you can make one additional attack against that creature as a part of that action.

subclassFeature.name: Mark of the Stalker
entries: While you are hidden from the target of your Ranger's Quarry feature, the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} you make each round against that creature does not automatically reveal your presence to that creature. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) check contested by your target's Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check. On a success, you remain hidden. If you are less than 30 feet from your target, the Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) check is made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

subclassFeature.name: Concealment
entries: You've become adept at evading creatures that rely on {@spell Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision}. While in {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}, you are {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible} to any creature that relies on {@spell Darkvision|sw5e-phb|darkvision} to see you in that {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}.

Additionally, when you hit a creature with a ranged {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} while hidden, you can force that creature to make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your tech save DC. On a failed save, the creature's {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn. You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Stalker's Flurry
entries: If you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against a target on your turn, you can forgo that {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} to immediately make an additional {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} against the same target as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Stalker's Dodge
entries: Whenever a creature attacks you and does not have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the creature's {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} against you. You can use this feature before or after the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} is made, but it must be used before the outcome of the roll is determined.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Focus
entries: The ways of the Force can reveal themselves to a sentinel through intense {@variantrule Concentration|sw5e-phb|concentration} and, most importantly, focus. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Focus use debilitating bursts of {@item Lightsaber|sw5e-phb|lightsaber} strikes and {@book force powers|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} to exhaust their foes, crushing any hopes they had of mounting an effective defense.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Burst
entries: You learn the {@i burst} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, you can use The Double Strike Force-Empowered Self options when you cast it as your action. If more than one creature would be affected, only one creature takes the additional damage. Finally, you add your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1) to damage rolls with it, and creatures that succeed on their {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} take half damage, instead of none.

subclassFeature.name: Blade Dance
entries: When you deal damage to a creature within 5 feet of you, you can move up to 10 feet without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|sw5e-phb|opportunity attacks}.

subclassFeature.name: Blade Storm
entries: Your bursts become even more overwhelming. Once on your turn, when a creature takes damage from you twice, you can immediately make one additional attack against that creature (no action required). This attack uses your Kinetic Combat die instead of the weapon's damage die.

subclassFeature.name: Focused Flow
entries: Whenever you use a Force-Empowered Self feature, you may instead expend no force points and roll a {@dice d4} in place of your Kinetic Combat die.

subclassFeature.name: Master Strike
entries: At 18th level, your bursts can overpower even the fiercest of foes. Once on your turn, when a creature takes damage from  you three times, you can force it to make a Constitution {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against your universal force save DC. On a failed save, it becomes {@condition Stunned|sw5e-phb|stunned} until the end of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Shadows
entries: In {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}, there is protection. Those sentinels who follow the Path of Shadows utilize a calculated plan, becoming masters of stealth and ambush who forgo the head-on attack for the vulnerable flank.

subclassFeature.name: Dead Silence
entries: You learn the {@i psychic charge} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, you can use Wisdom or Charisma as your {@book forcecasting ability|sw5e-phb|10|Forcecasting Ability} for it, and when you hit a creature with the {@i psychic charge} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers} and the target tries to speak, it takes additional damage equal to your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1), and its voice does not produce sound until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Cloak of Shadows
entries: You can take the {@action Hide|sw5e-phb} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn. Additionally, you can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Strike
entries: You learn to strike from the shadows. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the roll.
The extra damage increases to 2d6 at 11th level and 3d6 at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow Step
entries: You gain the ability to step from one shadow into another. While you are in dim light or {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or {@spell Darkness|sw5e-phb|darkness}. You then have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the first melee attack you make before the end of the turn.

subclassFeature.name: Shadow's Wrath
entries: Your training has taught you advanced techniques while you {@book maneuver|sw5e-phb|13|Maneuvers} in the shadows. While you are hidden from your target, the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} you make each round does not automatically reveal your presence. Make a Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|sw5e-phb}) check against your target's Wisdom ({@skill Perception|sw5e-phb}) check. On a success, you remain hidden. If you are also {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible}, you remain {@condition Invisible|sw5e-phb|invisible}.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Corsair
entries: There may come a time when a sentinel finds themselves stranded, hunted, or in any situation where they must hide their nature as a force wielder. Those sentinels who follow the Path of the Corsair make use of alternative weaponry not commonly associated with force-wielders to great effect.

subclassFeature.name: Bonus Proficiencies
entries: You gain proficiency with demolitions kits and three {@filter blasters|items|firearm=true} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Corsair Munitions
entries: You can throw grenades and set mines with your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}, instead of your action. Additionally, when you throw a grenade, you can use Wisdom or Charisma instead of Strength when determining your throwing range. Lastly, when determining the save DC of a {@optfeature Charge|sw5e-phb|charge}, grenade, mine, missile, or rocket you control, you can use your universal force save DC, if it would be higher than the item's DC.

subclassFeature.name: Force-Empowered Detonators
entries: You learn to create a number of small but potent grenades. Over the course of a short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}, you can create two grenades. You must have a {@item Demolitions kit|sw5e-phb|demolitions kit} in order to create these grenades. Your grenades can only be used by you, and they lose their potency at the end of your next short or {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

Your grenades can be set to detonate on impact or with a timer that causes them to explode on {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} count 20 (losing all {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} ties). As an action, you can prime and throw one of these grenade at a point you can see within 30 feet + your Strength modifier x 5. Each creature within 5 feet must make a Dexterity, Constitution, or Wisdom {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (your choice when you generate the grenade) against your universal force save DC. A creature takes damage using your Kinetic Combat die + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice) on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. The damage is force for Dexterity, necrotic for Constitution, or psychic for Wisdom.
You can make additional grenades at higher level: three at 5th level, four at 9th level, five at 13th level, and six at 17th level.

subclassFeature.name: Remote Start
entries: You learn to easily detonate primed explosives. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn, you can detonate a primed explosive you can see within 60 feet. Alternatively, if you take the {@action Attack|sw5e-phb} action on your turn and you are wielding a {@filter blaster|items|firearm=true} weapon with which you are proficient, you can choose to shoot the explosive rather than use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to detonate it as long as you wouldn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.
When you do so, the explosive immediately detonates, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the damage roll you make with that explosive.

subclassFeature.name: Energized Kinetics
entries: Once per turn, when you deal damage with a Force-Empowered Detonator or your Double Strike feature, you can deal additional damage using your Kinetic Combat die. The damage type is force, lightning, necrotic, or psychic (your choice).

subclassFeature.name: Disorienting Detonations
entries: When a creature fails the {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} against a Force-Empowered Detonator, you can spend 2 force points to subject it to one of the following conditions until the end of your next turn: {@condition Blinded|sw5e-phb|blinded}, {@condition Deafened|sw5e-phb|deafened}, {@condition Ignited|sw5e-phb|ignited} (1d12), {@condition Shocked|sw5e-phb|shocked}, or {@condition Slowed|sw5e-phb|slowed}.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Forceblade
entries: Some few master their weapon in ways that differ from their peers. Those sentinels who follow the Path of the Forceblade channel the Force into their weapon, forming a unique connection that grants you greater control over the weapon; it becomes an extension of their will.

subclassFeature.name: Phasethrow
entries: You learn the {@i saber throw} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, which does not count against your total powers known. Additionally, you no longer have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} with it if you are within 5 feet of a hostile creature, and you can use the Double Strike Force-Empowered Self options when you cast it as your action and hit a target. Finally, when you hit a creature with the {@i saber throw} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you deal additional damage equal to half your Wisdom or Charisma modifier (your choice, minimum of +1) if it doesn't already include that modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Forceblade Bond
entries: You learn how to bond with a light- or vibro-weapon through the Force, making it part of you.

You {@optfeature Perform|sw5e-phb|perform} the ritual over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a {@variantrule Short Rest|sw5e-phb|short rest}. The weapon must be within your reach throughout the ritual, at the conclusion of which you touch the weapon and forge the bond, gaining the following benefits:

items: You can't be disarmed of that weapon while you are conscious.

If the weapon is within 60 feet of you and you can see it, you can summon that weapon as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} on your turn, causing it to travel instantly to you. If you have a free hand, you catch the weapon. Otherwise, it lands at your feet.
You can use Wisdom or Charisma instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls.

entries: You can have two weapons bonded to you in this way at a time, and you can summon both of them to you with the same {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb}.

subclassFeature.name: Twin Saber Throw
entries: When you cast {@i saber throw} while wielding your forceblade, you can attack the same target multiple times.

Additionally, when you deal damage to a creature within 30 feet of you with your forceblade, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to teleport to within 5 feet of that creature and make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against that creature. This attack uses your Kinetic Combat die instead of your weapon's damage die. You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Twin Saber Throw
entries: When you cast {@i saber throw} while wielding your forceblade, you can attack the same target multiple times.

Additionally, when you deal damage to a creature within 30 feet of you with your forceblade, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to teleport to within 5 feet of that creature and make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against that creature. This attack uses your Kinetic Combat die instead of your weapon's damage die. You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

This attack uses your Kinetic Combat die instead of your weapon's damage die. You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Twin Saber Throw
entries: When you cast {@i saber throw} while wielding your forceblade, you can attack the same target multiple times.

Additionally, when you deal damage to a creature within 30 feet of you with your forceblade, you can use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|sw5e-phb} to teleport to within 5 feet of that creature and make a {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|melee weapon attack} against that creature. This attack uses your Kinetic Combat die instead of your weapon's damage die. You can use this feature three times. You gain an additional use at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. You regain all expended uses when you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|sw5e-phb|long rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Disruptive Throw
entries: When you are the target of a ranged attack, and the source is within range of your {@i saber throw} {@book force power|sw5e-phb|11|Force Powers}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|sw5e-phb} to throw your forceblade at the source of the attack. Make a ranged force attack. On a hit, this attack deals damage using your Kinetic Combat die instead of the weapon's damage die and you impose {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the triggering {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll}.

subclassFeature.name: Forceblade Mastery
entries: You've mastered controlling your forceblade with your mind, using it to keep your enemies at bay. As an action, you can telekinetically control your forceblade and have it strike any number of creatures within 10 feet of you, spending 1 force point per target. Each target must make a Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw} (DC = 8 + your bonus to {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack rolls} with that weapon). On a failed save, it takes damage using your Kinetic Combat die + half your sentinel level, is pushed back 10 feet and knocked prone.
